SetupReadme: First-run setup exists so that launching the desktop shell is the whole
installation procedure. On startup the gateway runs the platform's own
'chaos status --json', and if the database is empty it runs the
platform's own 'chaos init-db' and 'chaos load-all --skip-missing'.
GET /host/setup reports the whole thing; POST /host/setup/run repeats it.
It never drops, truncates or migrates. A database that already holds rows
but is missing declared tables, or a registry that is only partly loaded,
ends as 'needs_attention' with an explanation and no changes - this
database holds the homestead's alarm and telemetry history.
AutoSetup=false is for a node an operator manages by hand: the gateway
then neither reads nor writes the platform database on its own, and
/host/setup reports 'not_started'. POST /host/setup/run?force=true still
works, because an explicit request is an explicit request.
DatabaseUrl and DataDirectory are OVERRIDES. Left empty, the platform
uses its own defaults and the gateway reports what the platform says it
used rather than guessing.
TWO CHAOS_ NAMESPACES SHARE ONE PREFIX. This gateway binds
CHAOS_<PascalCase> (CHAOS_AutoSetup, CHAOS_DatabaseUrl). The Python
platform binds CHAOS_<SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE> (CHAOS_DATABASE_URL,
CHAOS_DATA_DIR). The underscores keep them apart, so no gateway setting
may ever be named with an underscore in it.
This key is ignored by the binder and exists only so the shape is
documented where an operator will look for it.
RoutesReadme: Route ownership is the migration seam. The compiled-in manifest is in
Chaos.Host/Routing/RouteOwnershipDefaults.cs and today marks every /api/v1
prefix as Python. GET /host/routes on a running host is the authoritative
live view - prefer it over reading this file.
Rows listed under Routes are merged over the compiled-in manifest by
PathPrefix. Porting a subsystem to .NET is one row:
"Routes": [
"PathPrefix": "/api/v1/alarms/definitions",
"Owner": "Dotnet",
"PortedInVersion": "0.6.0",
"Notes": "Alarm definitions served natively; the rest of /api/v1/alarms is still Python."
Matching is longest-prefix-wins at segment boundaries, so the row above
takes /api/v1/alarms/definitions and everything below it while
/api/v1/alarms/active keeps going to Python.
The host REFUSES TO START if a row says Dotnet and no .NET endpoint is
registered under that prefix. That is deliberate: a route marked ported
with nothing behind it answers 404, and a 404 from an alarm endpoint
reads like 'no alarms'.
This key is ignored by the binder and exists only so the shape is
documented where an operator will look for it.
